ei.title: Analysis — 인공 신경망의 지도 학습(오류 역전파) 메커니즘과 학습의 느림
ei.subject: 올림포스독해의기본2

fullPassage: Most artificial neural networks used in present-day artificial intelligence, despite their millions of inputs, outputs, and adjustable parameters, operate just like our proverbial hunter: they observe their errors and use them to adjust their internal state in the direction that they feel is best able to reduce the errors. In many cases, such learning is tightly guided. We tell the network exactly which response it should have activated at the output ("it is a 1, not a 7"), and we know precisely in which direction to adjust the parameters if they lead to an error (a mathematical calculation makes it possible to know exactly which connections to modify when the network activates the output "7" too often in response to an image of the number 1). In machine learning parlance, this situation is known as "supervised learning" (because someone, who can be likened to a supervisor, knows the correct answer that the system must give) and "error backpropagation" (because error signals are sent back into the network in order to modify its parameters). The procedure is simple: I try an answer, I am told what I should have answered, I measure my error, and I adjust my parameters to reduce it. At each step, I make only a small correction in the right direction. That's why such computer-based learning can be incredibly slow: learning a complex activity, like playing Tetris, requires applying this recipe thousands, millions, even billions of times. In a space that includes a multitude of adjustable parameters, it can take a long time to discover the optimal setting for every nut and bolt.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

❌ ③ guided: 'such learning is tightly guided' — be동사 + 과거분사 수동태. 정상

❌ ④ sent: 'error signals are sent back into the network' — be동사 + 과거분사 수동태. 정상

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ measuring → measure: 'I try ~, I am told ~, I measure ~, and I adjust ~'로 이어지는 병렬 구조의 본동사 자리. 앞뒤가 모두 현재시제 정동사이므로 measure가 맞음. 분사 measuring은 본동사가 될 수 없음.
det.analysis:
❌ ① reduce: 'is best able to reduce the errors' — be able to + 동사원형. 정상

❌ ② possible: 'makes it possible to know' — make + 가목적어 it + 형용사 possible + to부정사. 정상

✅ ③ measuring(오류) → measure: 'I try an answer, I am told ..., I measure my error, and I adjust ...' — 주어 I에 이어지는 병렬된 현재시제 본동사들. measure여야 하며 분사형 measuring은 정동사 역할 불가 ← 정답

det.tip: A, B, C, and D 병렬에서는 모든 요소의 형태를 맞춘다. try/am told/measure/adjust 모두 정동사.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ fast → slow: 뒤에 '이 절차를 수천, 수백만, 심지어 수십억 번 적용해야 한다'는 설명이 이어지므로 학습은 '느린(slow)' 것. fast(빠른)는 문맥과 모순.
det.analysis:
❌ ① reduce: 'best able to reduce the errors' — 신경망은 오류를 '줄이는' 방향으로 조정. 문맥 적절

❌ ② guided: 'such learning is tightly guided' — 정답을 알려주는 지도 학습이므로 '안내되는(guided)'. 적절

❌ ③ correct: 'knows the correct answer' — 감독자가 '올바른(correct)' 답을 앎. 적절

✅ ④ fast(오류) → slow: 'such computer-based learning can be incredibly fast: ... requires applying this recipe thousands, millions, even billions of times' — 수십억 번 반복이 필요하므로 '느린(slow)'이어야 함. fast는 모순 ← 정답
det.tip: 콜론(:) 뒤 '수십억 번 반복'이 단서. 느린(slow) 학습이어야 논리가 맞음.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ② increase → reduce: 신경망은 오류를 '줄이는(reduce)' 방향으로 내부 상태를 조정함. increase(늘리다)는 오류를 줄이려는 학습 목적과 정반대라 부적절.
det.analysis:
❌ ① observe: 'they observe their errors' — 신경망이 오류를 '관찰한다'. 문맥 적절

✅ ② increase(오류) → reduce: 'adjust their internal state in the direction that they feel is best able to increase the errors' — 학습의 목적은 오류를 '줄이는(reduce)' 것. increase(늘리다)는 정반대 ← 정답

❌ ③ guided: 'such learning is tightly guided' — 정답을 알려주는 지도 학습. 적절

❌ ④ small: 'I make only a small correction' — 각 단계에서 '작은(small)' 수정만 하므로 학습이 느림. 적절
det.tip: 오류를 가장 잘 'reduce(줄일)' 수 있는 방향. increase(늘리다)와 반대 개념.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ① reduce the errors(오류를 줄이다): 신경망은 오류를 관찰하고 그것을 이용해 내부 상태를 조정하는데, 그 방향은 오류를 '가장 잘 줄일 수 있다'고 느끼는 쪽. 따라서 빈칸은 '오류를 줄이다'.
det.analysis:
✅ ① reduce the errors(오류를 줄이다): 'observe their errors and use them to adjust their internal state in the direction that they feel is best able to ______' — 오류를 관찰·활용해 조정하는 목적은 오류를 줄이는 것 ← 정답

❌ ② memorize every input(모든 입력을 암기하다): 암기가 아니라 오류 기반 조정이 핵심

❌ ③ avoid any correction(어떤 수정도 피하다): 신경망은 끊임없이 수정하므로 정반대

❌ ④ imitate human hunters(인간 사냥꾼을 모방하다): 사냥꾼은 비유일 뿐, 모방이 목적이 아님
det.tip: 앞의 'observe their errors'와 'best able to'가 단서. 오류를 줄이는 방향으로 조정.

det.korean: ③ incredibly slow(엄청나게 느린): 빈칸 뒤 콜론에서 '테트리스 같은 복잡한 활동 학습은 이 절차를 수천, 수백만, 수십억 번 적용해야 한다'고 설명하므로 학습은 매우 '느린' 것.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

questions.passage: Most artificial neural networks used in present-day artificial intelligence, despite their millions of inputs, outputs, and adjustable parameters, operate just like our proverbial hunter: they observe their errors and use them to adjust their internal state in the direction that they feel is best able to reduce the errors. In many cases, such learning is tightly guided. We tell the network exactly which response it should have activated at the output ("it is a 1, not a 7"), and we know precisely in which direction to adjust the parameters if they lead to an error (a mathematical calculation makes it possible to know exactly which connections to modify when the network activates the output "7" too often in response to an image of the number 1). In machine learning parlance, this situation is known as "supervised learning" (because someone, who can be likened to a supervisor, knows the correct answer that the system must give) and "error backpropagation" (because error signals are sent back into the network in order to modify its parameters). The procedure is simple: I try an answer, I am told what I should have answered, I measure my error, and I adjust my parameters to reduce it. At each step, I make only a small correction in the right direction. That's why such computer-based learning can be incredibly slow: learning a complex activity, like playing Tetris, requires applying this recipe thousands, millions, even billions of times. In a space that includes a multitude of adjustable parameters, it can take a long time to discover the optimal setting for every nut and bolt.

det.tip: thousands, millions, even billions of times = 수없이 반복. '한 번'은 불일치.

questions.passage: Most artificial neural networks used in present-day artificial intelligence, despite their millions of inputs, outputs, and adjustable parameters, operate just like our proverbial hunter: __________ in the direction that they feel is best able to reduce the errors. In many cases, such learning is tightly guided. We tell the network exactly which response it should have activated at the output ("it is a 1, not a 7"), and we know precisely in which direction to adjust the parameters if they lead to an error (a mathematical calculation makes it possible to know exactly which connections to modify when the network activates the output "7" too often in response to an image of the number 1). In machine learning parlance, this situation is known as "supervised learning" (because someone, who can be likened to a supervisor, knows the correct answer that the system must give) and "error backpropagation" (because error signals are sent back into the network in order to modify its parameters). The procedure is simple: I try an answer, I am told what I should have answered, I measure my error, and I adjust my parameters to reduce it. At each step, I make only a small correction in the right direction. That's why such computer-based learning can be incredibly slow: learning a complex activity, like playing Tetris, requires applying this recipe thousands, millions, even billions of times. In a space that includes a multitude of adjustable parameters, it can take a long time to discover the optimal setting for every nut and bolt.

det.analysis:
본문 첫 문장: 'they observe their errors and use them to adjust their internal state in the direction ...'. 빈칸은 이 절.

배열 순서:

- and use them: 그리고 그것들을 사용한다(and로 연결된 두 번째 동사, them = errors)
- to adjust their internal state: 내부 상태를 조정하기 위해(목적의 to부정사)

the가 아닌 their가 두 번(their errors / their internal state) 쓰이는 점에 유의. 총 12단어.
det.tip: observe A and use B to adjust C 구조. their가 두 번(오류, 내부 상태) 쓰인다.
